description: This file implements various HTTP security schemes for FastAPI, including Basic, Bearer, Digest authentication, and utility classes for handling credentials and errors.

classes.name: HTTPBasicCredentials
classes.description: Data model representing HTTP Basic authentication credentials with username and password.

classes.name: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials
classes.description: Data model representing HTTP authorization scheme and credentials, used in Bearer and Digest schemes.

classes.name: HTTPBase
classes.description: Base class for HTTP authentication schemes, providing common methods for handling authorization headers and errors.

classes.name: HTTPBasic
classes.description: Implementation of Basic Authentication scheme, decoding credentials from the Authorization header.

classes.name: HTTPBearer
classes.description: Implementation of Bearer Token authentication scheme, extracting token from the Authorization header.

classes.name: HTTPDigest
classes.description: Stub implementation of Digest authentication, designed for integration with OpenAPI; does not fully implement the scheme.

methods.name: dict[str,str] make_authenticate_headers(self)
methods.description: Generates appropriate WWW-Authenticate headers for the authentication scheme.

methods.name: HTTPException make_not_authenticated_error(self)
methods.description: Creates an HTTP 401 Unauthorized exception with proper headers.

methods.name: Optional[HTTPBasicCredentials] __call__( self, request: Request )
methods.description: Asynchronous method to extract and validate the credentials from request headers.

                " ), ] = None, auto_error: Annotated[ bool, Doc( "
                By default, if the HTTP Bearer token is not provided (in an
                `Authorization` header), `HTTPBearer` will automatically cancel the
                request and send the client an error.

                If `auto_error` is set to `False`, when the HTTP Bearer token
                is not available, instead of erroring out, the dependency result will
                be `None`.

                This is useful when you want to have optional authentication.

                It is also useful when you want to have authentication that can be
                provided in one of multiple optional ways (for example, in an HTTP
                Bearer token or in a cookie).
